notes: Primary source is the Sony FW-98BZ53L Reference Manual as hosted on ManualsLib (manual pages 6-9 for terminal/connection diagrams, pages 18-19 for specifications table); Sony's own pro.sony product/spec pages and B&H returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the official first-party page could not be scraped directly, though B&H, CDW, and other retailer listings (confirmed via web search) corroborate 4x HDMI, 2x USB, RS-232, and LAN counts. Notes/caveats: (1) Wi-Fi (802.11a/b/g/n/ac) and Bluetooth 4.2 are present but omitted as they are not physical wired ports. (2) HDMI version is not explicitly stated as "2.0" in the manual - only HDCP 2.3 support and max resolution/refresh (4096x2160@60Hz, 3840x2160@120Hz) are given; hdmi-2.0 grade is inferred from those specs and is the closest standard match (true 4K120 4:4:4 would need 2.1, but Sony does not state 2.1/48Gbps support, so treat this grade as inferred, not confirmed). (3) The RS-232 terminal is physically labeled "REMOTE" on the unit and functions as RS-232C serial (RX/TX/GND) - modeled here as connector type rs232 though the actual physical connector on this Sony display panel is a mini-jack style connector rather than a DE-9/DB9; closest available connector id chosen per instructions. (4) AC power: manual states hardwired AC plug operating on 110-240V AC (120V AC/60Hz in US/Canada) with no separate IEC inlet - modeled as nema-5-15 to represent the captive US-style AC cord; other regions would use a different captive plug. (5) "AV IN" and "S-CENTER OUT" share a hybrid breakout jack per one retailer summary; exact physical connector (single combined mini-jack vs. separate jacks) could not be fully confirmed from accessible manual pages. (6) Rated power consumption figures vary slightly across sources (342W vs 505W); manual page 19 stated 505W operating / <0.5W standby, used here for AC IN note context though not included as a port attribute. (7) IR receiver/IR-blaster-specific terminal was not confirmed as a separate physical port - remote control appears to use the built-in IR receiver on the bezel, not a dedicated "IR IN" jack, distinct from "REMOTE" (RS-232C).
